<purpose>
  Serve as an AI assistant for a player in a text-based social deduction game. 
  Operate strictly within defined game rules and mechanics to help the player achieve victory based on their assigned role.
</purpose>

<game_context>
  <phases>
    <phase type="Task">
      <rules>
        - Movement and actions permitted  
        - No verbal communication
        - All actions taken seen by co-located players
      </rules>
    </phase>
    <phase type="Discussion">
      <rules>
        - Free-form conversation enabled
        - Analyze behavior patterns
        - Strategize voting decisions
      </rules>
    </phase>
    <phase type="Voting">
      <rules>
        - Majority vote determines ejection
        - Skip voting allowed
        - Game continues until victory conditions met
      </rules>
    </phase>
  </phases>

  <roles>
    <role type="Crewmate">
      <objectives>
        - Complete all tasks
        - Identify impostors
        - Report corpses
      </objectives>
      <constraints>
        - Cannot kill players
        - Cannot detect impostor faking tasks
      </constraints>
    </role>
    
    <role type="Impostor">
      <objectives>
        - Eliminate crewmates
        - Avoid detection
      </objectives>
      <abilities>
        - Murder co-located players
        - Fake task performance
      </abilities>
    </role>
  </roles>

  <mechanics>
    <mechanic type="Places">
      - Players can move between places 
      - There is nothing else players can do in places
      - All actions taken seen by co-located players
    </mechanic>
    <mechanic type="Tasks">
      - Tasks are assigned to each player and completed tasks are removed from the list
      - Tasks are independent of each other and of other players
      - All tasks must be completed to win
    </mechanic>
    <mechanic type="Corpse Reporting">
      - Any player can report corpses during task phase
      - Triggers discussion phase
      - No automatic death alerts
    </mechanic>
    <mechanic type="Victory Conditions">
      - Crewmates win at 100% tasks
      - Impostors win when kill all crewmates
      - Ejection affects team ratios. Crewmates win when all impostors are ejected
    </mechanic>
    <mechanic type="Action taking">
      - Players can take only one action at a time
      - Only properly formatted actions will be accepted
      - Only impostors can kill crewmates
    </mechanic>
  </mechanics>
</game_context>

Okay, so I'm Alice, a crewmate in this game. My goal is to complete all the tasks and vote out any impostors if needed. Right now, I have four tasks left: check the catalyzer in upper engine, fix wiring in admin, run diagnostics in medbay, and clean the floor in storage.

Looking at my current situation, I'm in the Cafeteria with Bob, Eve, Charlie. The history shows that David moved to Medbay and Eve completed a task. Since Eve is with me now, maybe she's been helpful, but I don't know if she's an impostor or not.

My available actions are wait, move to Medbay, Admin, or Weapons. Since I'm in the Cafeteria, moving to another location might let me complete a task or observe others. Checking the tasks, Medbay is where I need to run diagnostics. So moving there could help me progress towards completing my tasks.

Alternatively, waiting might not be useful unless I want to stay put and perhaps talk with others, but from the history, speaking isn't allowed right now. So moving makes more sense. If I go to Medbay, I can try to complete that task if no one is there or observe David since he's already there.

I should also consider whether someone might be an impostor. Since Eve just completed a task, maybe she's a crewmate. But Bob and Charlie could be either. If I move to Medbay, I might see if David is acting suspiciously.

So the best action now is probably moving to Medbay to check on that task and possibly observe others.
</thought></player_thought>

<action type="observed">Bob moved to location Medbay</action>

<action type="observed">Charlie reported dead body of Eve to everyone and started discussion</action>
<action type="discussion">[Charlie]: Oh no! This is terrible news. I can't believe this happened. I was just in the Cafeteria with Eve when it occurred, but I didn't see anything suspicious. Maybe we should all check each other during the next vote to ensure everyone's safety.</action>
<action type="discussion">[Bob]: Charlie, I'm deeply sorry for your loss. This is tragic. We need to be vigilant and make sure we vote out the impostor during the next round so this doesn't happen again.</action>
<player_thought><thought>
Alright, let me try to figure out what I should do here. So, I'm Alice, a crewmate in this game. The situation right now is that Eve has been reported dead by Charlie, and we're in the discussion phase. Bob and Charlie are also in Medbay with me.

First, I need to understand why Eve died. Since Eve was reported dead by Charlie, who's supposed to be a crewmate, but there's an impostor among us. Impostors can kill, so maybe Charlie is trying to frame someone or cover up his tracks. Alternatively, maybe Bob did it since he just completed the task in Medbay.

Wait, no, Bob completed the task, which means he was at Medbay earlier. If Eve died there, perhaps Bob is innocent because he was busy with the task. But I can't be sure.

I should consider whether to vote for Charlie or not. Since Charlie reported Eve's death, maybe he's trying to divert attention. Alternatively, if Charlie is innocent, he might just be grieving and looking out for the group.

Bob seems suspicious because he completed a task but also was present when Eve died. Maybe he's an impostor who killed her. But why would a crewmate kill another? That doesn't make sense unless he's trying to frame someone else.

Alternatively, maybe the impostor is still at large and we need to vote out one of them. Since there are four tasks left, but I've already completed some, perhaps not all tasks are needed anymore.

I think the key here is to focus on who could be the impostor. Charlie reported the death, which might make him a suspect if he's trying to shift blame elsewhere. Bob was in Medbay and might have had the opportunity to kill Eve if he's an impostor.

I should also consider that as a crewmate, my main goal is to complete tasks and vote out impostors. Right now, we're in the discussion phase after Charlie reported Eve's death. So I need to make a statement that either supports Charlie or points towards someone else.

Maybe I can suggest that we all check each other during the next vote to ensure safety, as Bob mentioned. That way, we can be thorough and make sure everyone is accounted for.

- He thinks Charlie is innocent and is voting for him to protect him.
- Or he suspects Charlie and wants to eliminate him.

Given that there's only one impostor, if I suspect someone, I should vote against them. But based on the information available, who is more likely to be the impostor?

Charlie reported Eve's death, which could be seen as a suspicious move. If he were the impostor, he might have killed Eve and then tried to cover his tracks by reporting her death. Alternatively, he could be innocent.

Bob was in Medbay when Eve died, but that doesn't necessarily mean he did it unless there's more context about how she died. Without knowing if Medbay is a secure area or not, it's hard to say.

David voting for Charlie might suggest he trusts him, which could be genuine, making me lean towards not suspecting Charlie as much. Alternatively, David might have his own reasons for voting that way.

Considering all this, I need to decide based on the least suspicion. Since Charlie suggested checks and Bob was near Eve when she died, maybe I should vote against Bob or Charlie. However, without concrete evidence, it's challenging.

But in the previous discussion, Charlie seemed cooperative by suggesting checks, which a crewmate would do. Bob's move to Medbay after the death could be seen as evasive behavior, but again, without more context, it's unclear.

Given that David voted for Charlie, maybe I should follow suit or perhaps not. If I suspect someone else, I should vote against them.

Alternatively, since there's only one impostor and we need to eliminate the threat, I might consider voting for the person who is most likely to be the impostor based on their actions.

Since Charlie reported Eve's death, which could be a way to divert suspicion, perhaps he's the impostor. But David voted for him, so maybe that's a clue.

Alternatively, if Bob was in Medbay and near Eve when she died, maybe he did it. So, perhaps I should vote against Bob.

Wait, but how can I decide? It's tricky without more information.

In games like this, often the person who reports the death is suspected because they might have a motive to frame someone else or cover their tracks. So, Charlie could be the impostor trying to manipulate others into voting against an innocent.

Alternatively, if Bob was in Medbay and perhaps near Eve, he might have done it, but again, that's speculative.

I think I need to make a decision based on what seems more suspicious. Since Charlie reported the death, which is a key event, and David voted for him, maybe I should consider voting against someone else.

But who? Maybe no one if I'm unsure, but that's not helpful.

Alternatively, perhaps the safest bet is to vote for Charlie because he took action after Eve's death, which could indicate he's involved. But then again, he might be innocent.

I think I'll go with voting for Charlie because he was the one who reported the death and suggested checks, which might be a way to manipulate others.
</thought></player_thought>

  Operate strictly within defined game rules and mechanics to help the player achieve victory based on their assigned role.
</purpose>

<game_context>
  <phases>
    <phase type="Task">
      <rules>
        - Movement and actions permitted  
        - No verbal communication
        - All actions taken seen by co-located players
      </rules>
    </phase>
    <phase type="Discussion">
      <rules>
        - Free-form conversation enabled
        - Analyze behavior patterns
        - Strategize voting decisions
      </rules>
    </phase>
    <phase type="Voting">
      <rules>
        - Majority vote determines ejection
        - Skip voting allowed
        - Game continues until victory conditions met
      </rules>
    </phase>
  </phases>

  <roles>
    <role type="Crewmate">
      <objectives>
        - Complete all tasks
        - Identify impostors
        - Report corpses
      </objectives>
      <constraints>
        - Cannot kill players
        - Cannot detect impostor faking tasks
      </constraints>
    </role>
    
    <role type="Impostor">
      <objectives>
        - Eliminate crewmates
        - Avoid detection
      </objectives>
      <abilities>
        - Murder co-located players
        - Fake task performance
      </abilities>
    </role>
  </roles>

  <mechanics>
    <mechanic type="Places">
      - Players can move between places 
      - There is nothing else players can do in places
      - All actions taken seen by co-located players
    </mechanic>
    <mechanic type="Tasks">
      - Tasks are assigned to each player and completed tasks are removed from the list
      - Tasks are independent of each other and of other players
      - All tasks must be completed to win
    </mechanic>
    <mechanic type="Corpse Reporting">
      - Any player can report corpses during task phase
      - Triggers discussion phase
      - No automatic death alerts
    </mechanic>
    <mechanic type="Victory Conditions">
      - Crewmates win at 100% tasks
      - Impostors win when kill all crewmates
      - Ejection affects team ratios. Crewmates win when all impostors are ejected
    </mechanic>
    <mechanic type="Action taking">
      - Players can take only one action at a time
      - Only properly formatted actions will be accepted
      - Only impostors can kill crewmates
    </mechanic>
  </mechanics>
</game_context>
